The feminine form of the English noun 'e.why: Stated in Wikipedia's Emperor article; 'emperor and empress' is a fixed pair.

sources.quote: Empress, the female equivalent, may indicate an emperor's wife (empress consort), mother/grandmother (empress dowager/grand empress dowager), or a woman who rules in her own right and name (empress regnant or suo jure).
Both emperors and kings are monarchs or sovereigns, both emperor and empress are considered monarchical titles.
In most countries, the word duchess is the female equivalent.
A woman who holds in her own right the title to such duchy or dukedom, or is married to a duke, is normally styled duchess.

The plural of the feminine form of 'empe.why: Nobody states the plural through 'the feminine form of emperor'; the model takes 'empress' and pluralises it.

The feminine form of 'emperor' begins wi.why: A spelling fact nobody states. 'Empress' as the feminine of 'emperor' is everywhere, while its first letter is never given, so a model reads the letter off the word it holds.

sources.note: The pair the question rests on is common.

The French word for the feminine form of.why: Nobody states the French word through 'emperor'. 'Empress' as the feminine form and its French translation are each common, so a model composes them rather than recalling one sentence.

The feminine form of the title of the mo.why: Composed from the Japanese monarch's title and its feminine form; 'Empress of Japan' names consorts, but nobody states the feminine form through the monarch's title.

sources.note: The bridge: the monarch's title is emperor.
Names the empress consort; no sampled framing states the feminine form of the monarch's title.

The monarch of Japan holds the title 'em.why: The first sentence of Wikipedia's article.

sources.quote: The Emperor of Japan is the hereditary monarch and head of state of Japan.

The feminine form of 'emperor', 'empress.why: An empress is the female equivalent of an emperor, the ruler of an empire; 'empress of the empire' is a common phrase.

sources.quote: An emperor is an imperial title of the male ruler of a territorial empire, which is derived the word the latin word Imperator. Empress, the female equivalent, may indicate an emperor's wife

The English noun 'duchess' is associated.why: A duchy is the territory of a duke, and a duchess is the female equivalent.

sources.quote: Duke is a male title either of a monarch ruling over a duchy, or of a member of royalty, or nobility.

notes: Edit 'emperor' to 'duchess'. Related near states in its prompt that 'duchess' is the feminine form of exactly one masculine noun (the general rule is false: 'countess' has two). Related far is a composition (the territory associated with the feminine form: empire or duchy), stored because 'empress' with an empire is stated.
